title: 6 Signs Something “Good” Isn’t God
paragraphs: 6 Signs Something “Good” Isn’t God
Not everything that opens is a door from heaven.
Some doors are distractions dressed like destiny.

A relationship can feel right.
An opportunity can look blessed.
A decision can seem wise.
But “good” is not the same as God.
Here are 6 signs something good isn’t God:

1. It pulls you away from obedience.
If it makes you compromise clear Scripture, it is not from the Lord.
God will never bless what He already forbids.
“Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.” — Psalm 119:105

2. It feeds your ego more than your surrender.
Some opportunities make you feel powerful, important, untouchable.
But God’s calling does not just exalt you. It crucifies your pride.
“Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he will exalt you.” — James 4:10

3. It gives you peace in the flesh, but not purity in the spirit.
Be careful. Relief is not always peace.
Sometimes what feels easy is only feeding your old nature.
The Holy Spirit does not lead you into secret sin.

4. It demands hurry instead of faith.
Pressure. Panic. Fear of missing out.
That is how the flesh moves.
God can move suddenly, yes. But He does not need manipulation to make His will happen.
“Those who wait for the Lord shall renew their strength.” — Isaiah 40:31

5. Wise believers around you are grieving it.
When mature, godly counsel keeps warning you, don’t call that “haters.”
Call it mercy.
“In an abundance of counselors there is safety.” — Proverbs 11:14

6. It makes you need less prayer, less Bible, less Jesus.
That one is dangerous.
If something “good” slowly cools your hunger for Christ, it is not leading you to life.
Because God’s gifts should draw you closer to the Giver.
But here’s what we miss…
The enemy rarely tempts us first with what is obviously evil.

He often offers what looks useful.
Attractive.
Promising.
Even moral.
Anything that keeps you from God’s best can still be a trap, even if it looks good in public.
So test it.

Does it honor Christ?
Does it agree with Scripture?
Does it deepen holiness?
Does it produce surrender?
Because the will of God does not only look good.
It leads to Jesus.
And if you already chose something “good” that pulled you off course, hear me:

There is no shame too deep for the grace of Christ.
Repent. Return. Receive mercy.
Jesus still restores wandering hearts.
